result.reason: The redline does not match either playbook position. Although the general cap and damages exclusion are facially mutual and it adds confidentiality, gross-negligence and wilful-misconduct carve-outs, the cap is limited to amounts actually paid rather than the preferred greater-of formulation, and indemnification is not expressly carved out unless Section 8 happens to cover it. It also introduces non-playbook terms: a three-times-annual-fees cap for support and service breaches and an asymmetric rule treating Corio customer payments or credits as direct damages. Those changes are commercially material, unnecessary, and may undermine the consequential-damages exclusion. The treatment of all payment obligations as outside the cap is also broader and less precise than stating that Customer's payment obligations are not damages. Drafting quality is further reduced by retaining the duplicated, corrupted paragraph beginning '10 LIABILITY RELATES.'
